summary_en: Tokugawa Ieyasu's great castle, where the rebuilt Hommaru Palace glows with gold-leaf paintings. The main keep is closed for now.
description_en: The keep is closed for now, so come for the Hommaru Palace: a run of tatami rooms rebuilt with traditional joinery, their sliding doors painted with tigers, pheasants and cherry blossoms in the Kano-school style. Entry is included in the castle ticket.

Tokugawa Ieyasu ordered the castle built in 1610, and it was home to the Owari Tokugawa for more than two centuries. Air raids in May 1945 destroyed most of it; the keep, crowned with golden shachihoko, was rebuilt in concrete in 1959.

Allow one to two hours. Walk the stone walls and moats, find the Southwest Corner Watchtower — one of the few Edo-period buildings to survive the war — and come in late March or early April, when about 900 cherry trees bloom across the grounds.
highlights_en: Golden shachihoko on the keep roof
Free English tours at 12:30 most days
opening_hours: 9:00–16:30 (last entry 16:00). Adults ¥1,000 from 1 October 2026; junior high school age and under free.
access_en: 5-minute walk from Exit 7 of Nagoyajo Station on the Meijo subway line. The Me-guru sightseeing bus and city buses also stop at the main gate (Nagoyajo Seimon-mae). Free volunteer English tours start at 12:30 from the Main Gate and East Gate (not held 29 December – 4 January, and paused 22 June – 30 September in 2026).
